title: 5 Website Fixes to Make Over the Holiday Downtime
h1: Fix these 5 things on your site over the holidays
meta: Slow weeks? Fix the five things that actually lose you jobs: phone above the fold, fast load, clear service area, real photos, a reason to call now.
short: The five site fixes that actually move the needle, done over the slow weeks.
statLabel: site fixes that lose you jobs if skipped

body.answer: Use the holiday downtime to fix five things on your site: phone above the fold, fast load, clear service area, real photos, and a reason to call now.
body.html:
Your website doesn't need to be pretty. It needs to turn a visitor into a phone call. Most contractor sites fail at that in five specific, fixable ways. The slow weeks are the time to knock them out.

Open your own site on your phone right now and go down this list. No developer required for most of it.

body.h2: Phone above the fold, and fast load
body.answer: Put a tap-to-call number at the top where it shows without scrolling, and make sure the page loads in a couple seconds on a phone.
body.html:
Fix one: the phone number has to be at the top, visible without scrolling, and tap-to-call on a phone. If a homeowner has to hunt for how to reach you, they leave. This is the number one thing shops get wrong.

Fix two: speed. If your site takes five seconds to load on a phone, people bail before they see anything. Crush your image file sizes and cut the junk plugins. A slow site loses leads before you ever get the chance to answer fast — and answering fast is what wins them, since responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd).

body.h2: Clear service area and real photos
body.answer: Spell out the towns you serve in plain text, and swap stock photos for real shots of your crew, trucks, and work.
body.html:
Fix three: say where you work, in words. List the towns and counties you serve on the page. Homeowners want to know you actually come to them before they call, and it helps you show up when they search your area.

Fix four: kill the stock photos. The smiling model in a clean hard hat fools nobody. Put up real photos of your trucks, your crew, and finished jobs. Real photos build trust the way reviews do — and most homeowners read online reviews before choosing a contractor, and most won't seriously consider a shop under 4 stars (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey), so pair your photos with those reviews front and center.

body.h2: Give them a reason to call now
body.answer: Add a clear, specific reason to call today — fast response, free estimate, same-week scheduling — and back it with missed-call text-back.
body.html:
Fix five: a reason to act today. 'Free estimates,' 'same-week scheduling,' 'we answer the phone.' Something specific and true that pushes a maybe into a call. Vague beats nobody.

Then make sure that call actually lands. Set up missed-call text-back so a missed call gets an instant text instead of a dead end, and tighten your pickup speed per speed to lead for contractors. If you'd rather hand the whole site fix to a human, talk to Aaron.

faq.q: Do I need a whole new website?
faq.a: Almost never. These five fixes — phone, speed, service area, real photos, a reason to call — get you most of the way on the site you already have.
Phone number above the fold, tap-to-call. If people can't easily reach you, nothing else on the site matters.
Homeowners can spot them, and they build zero trust. Real photos of your crew and work do the job stock never will.
